construction: Original authored cubic paths; open intervals, soft pen turns and clipped terminals. No traced or raster geometry.

artworks.title: Section pause
artworks.brief: Two unequal pen rules pause around a deliberate empty interval. Use between substantial passages, never as a broken data axis.
artworks.optical_note: The 16px-height master uses a 7px central interval and removes long-scale waviness; widths are 64, 80 and 96px.

artworks.title: End stop
artworks.brief: A long quiet rule ends before a compact cut-nib lozenge. Signals a visual rest without replacing headings or semantic separators.
artworks.optical_note: The detached solid terminal remains over 3px across at the smallest size; it is not a miniature logo.

artworks.title: Margin stitch
artworks.brief: Two short unequal oblique pen cuts mark a passage in the margin. They do not mean pause, quotation or a mathematical operator.
artworks.optical_note: The two cuts are separated by more than a stroke width at 16px. Use one instance beside a labelled passage.

artworks.title: Margin fold
artworks.brief: An open page-corner turn, with a curled return and no enclosing page. A small companion to a note, never a bookmark control.
artworks.optical_note: At 16px the inner return is shortened and opened. The fold is a graphic metaphor, not a claim of physical foldability.

artworks.title: Note seat
artworks.brief: An asymmetric open saddle supports an adjacent note label. The text or native link carries identity and action; the mark is not a number container.
artworks.optical_note: The 16px bowl is broad and shallow; the left and right shoulders remain unequal at every optical size.

artworks.title: Paired cuts
artworks.brief: Two displaced corner cuts reserve an interval between related labels. Matching visible note numbers establish the relationship, not the corners alone.
artworks.optical_note: Open rather than a boxed badge; no shared center, circle, check or arrow. Never a selection or scan-target affordance.

artworks.title: Locator tab
artworks.brief: A small notched tab attaches a page, section or timestamp locator. Pair with Source recorded and the actual locator; no truth or verification claim.
artworks.optical_note: The notch is widened at 16px and the staff extends below the tab. This does not replace the archived chain-link source symbol.

artworks.title: Excerpt notch
artworks.brief: A folded short edge points toward two uneven excerpt rules. Only accompany an actual excerpt with attribution and locator; the rules are not text.
artworks.optical_note: Two clear rules survive at 16px. The open edge avoids the existing notebook and framed-figure silhouettes.

artworks.title: Interpretation seam
artworks.brief: Separated material strokes are bridged by one raised curve. Always pair with the existing Interpretation label; the bridge illustrates reasoning, not a proven implication.
artworks.optical_note: At 16px the base fragments are short and the bridge is flattened to keep the central gap clear. No data, causality or certainty is encoded.

artworks.title: Record gap
artworks.brief: An intentionally open record corner and a detached short entry stroke accompany an explicit missing or unchecked context. The open shape does not establish the reason for the gap.
artworks.optical_note: The missing upper-right corner stays conspicuously open. Not a checkbox, loading spinner, error badge or new evidence basis.

artworks.title: Leader landing
artworks.brief: A short leader stops before a shallow concave landing. It identifies a note's endpoint without an arrowhead. An existing layout owner must supply the measured connector and text relationship.
artworks.optical_note: The gap remains open at 16px; the landing is not a node, force arrow, measurement, port or knowledge-graph edge.

artworks.title: Extent ends
artworks.brief: Two short outward-swept terminals reserve an empty span for a labelled passage or region. They are annotation accents, never a dimension line, error bar or numerical interval.
artworks.optical_note: The ends use shallow curves rather than the existing curly brace or tall bracket. Keep a visible text description of the referenced region.
